newsitem.title: GHANA: ECOWAS threatens more sanctions on Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: ECOWAS threatens more sanctions on Sierra Leone.

text.p: Foreign ministers from four West African states said on Friday they would recommend that their heads of state impose tougher sanctions on the military junta of Sierra Leone at a summit meeting later this month.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has already imposed an air, land and sea blockade on Sierra Leone in an effort to force the junta to restore President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, ousted on May 25.

The ECOWAS summit in Abuja, Nigeria, from August 27 to 29 will consider other measures, but Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi refused to elaborate at a news conference held after a two-day meeting in the Ghanaian capital, Accra.
Ikimi condemned the latest fighting between ECOWAS troops and junta forces which has killed 15 people, most of them civilians, in and around the airport town of Lungi.
"It seems to be a pattern of the elements in Sierra Leone that any time talks are going on, they attack our men," Ikimi said.
He said the ECOWAS forces would not give up. "We have the backing of the international community. I hope they will give us the material support as well," he said.
He hinted that the ECOWAS ministers might consider releasing Foday Sankoh, leader of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF) rebel force that has rallied to the junta.
Sankoh is under effective house arrest in Nigeria, and junta leaders have demanded that he be released to take part in peace talks.
He was not allowed to travel to Abidjan, Ivory Coast, for talks that collapsed last month when the junta said it intended to stay in power for four years.
The Accra meeting was attended by ministers from Ghana, Ivory Coast and Guinea as well as Nigeria. These four countries have been mandated by ECOWAS to find a solution to the Sierra Leone crisis.
